title: Shortwave inference checklist — morning triage & kernel todo
body:
Quick morning capture — short experiment list + triage notes

Context: oncall handoff looked at elevated p99s on nvlink-heavy nodes overnight. Customer impact low (internal test traffic) but stack traces show repeated stalls in KV cache warm path. Taking an action-first approach before broader investigation.

Top-level goals for today:
- quarantine a reproducible case we can run locally (priority: unblock devs)
- run micro-bench to isolate whether stalls are CPU-bound, nvlink-related, or due to cache eviction thrashing
- leave clear runbook steps for oncall next shift

Immediate checklist (shortwave):
1) Reproduce locally
   - dataset: small prefix set from /data/latency-priming/2026-03-10/short-sessions.gz
   - command: ./run_local_infer.sh --model redwood-mistral-7B --seq 1024 --concurrency 6 --kv-warm 1 --log-events
   - note: use docker image rwinf/dev-infer:2026-03-09 to match node env

2) Capture perf and nvlink stats
   - perf: perf record -F 99 -g -- ./run_local_infer.sh ... then perf report (focus on memcpy, cudaMemcpy, kernel stalls)
   - nvlink: nvidia-smi nvlink --status and nvlink top counters (on node)
   - kernel logs: journalctl -u rwinf-runtime -n 500 | grep -i kv_cache

3) Hypotheses (quick, raw)
   - H1: KV cache eviction frequency spiking due to batch-size jitter -> causes repeated KV loads and PCIe/NVLink saturation
   - H2: A GC-like event in process alloc path causes short stop-the-world pauses when map grows -> thread preemption visible in perf stacks
   - H3: Driver firmware nvlink retry behavior under sustained small transfers -> weird retransmits appear as stalls

4) Short experiments to differentiate (order matters)
   - E1 (cheap): increase batch skew tolerance to 5ms in config and run for 20 minutes. If p99 drops quickly, points to batching/queueing effects.
   - E2: Force KV cache pinning for pinned-prefix set (set KV_CACHE_PIN=1) and run same workload. If lat >50% lower, eviction is suspect.
   - E3: Run with a kernel-level isolcpus mask for inference threads (isolcpus=2-5) to see if scheduler preemption is contributing. Measure with /proc/interrupts and top.

Observations from a quick curl to internal health endpoint (rwinf-node-03):
- /metrics shows steady token throughput but small bursts of request-queue-length ~3 every ~90s
- logs show repeated message: "kv_cache: miss while priming prefix 0x7f5e3 " at 03:14:22

Repro steps I saved (scratch):
- pull small trace: gsutil cp gs://rwinf-debug/shortwave/trace-20260310.tar.gz /tmp
- untar and run: tar -xzvf trace-20260310.tar.gz && ./replay_trace.sh trace.json --headroom 0.2
- if replay fails with mmap errors, try ulimit -n 65536; also set RLIMIT_MEMLOCK high for pinned pages

Mini TODOs (2-3 hour tasks):
- [ ] Run E1 and record p50/p90/p99 baseline (+ Samir)
- [ ] Kick E2 with pinned-cache flag on node-05 (use canary routing) (+ Ivy)
- [ ] Capture perf on a short run and attach perf script output to JIRA-4581

Notes-to-self / miscellaneous:
- remember to bump the local runtime to latest patch (2026-03-09) because older builds hide symbol names in perf output
- if we see repetitive nvlink retransmit logs, try forcing lower PCIe link speed to reproduce slower but clearer behavior (nodectl set-link-speed)
- consider adding a non-blocking KV prime path that returns a best-effort warm result instead of blocking the request; quick design sketch in slack: #eng-runtime -> thread

Handoff message (for next shift):
- what I ran: E1 toggled, saw 18% drop in p99 in 10m window (still noisy). E2 queued for node-05, pending. Perf capture started but incomplete (left running). Important logs: kv_cache miss spiking at 03:14.
- action items if p99 spike returns: revert canary to fallback model variant, escalate to infra for nvlink driver check, attach perf data to JIRA-4581 and notify Samir.

Open questions / followups:
- Are there any recent kernel upgrades on node-05? Check images and GRUB timestamps.
- Is this correlated with scheduled backups? (I saw rsync jobs around 02:45 last night)
- Can we add a small histogram metric for KV eviction-to-hit latency? Would help isolate whether eviction causes backpressure.

Raw scratch snippets (feel free to edit):
- "priming delay ~8-12ms when cache miss chain >3"
- "nvlink retransmit x3 seen in dmesg -> see driver tracepoints"
- "try isolating io threads to cpu set 10-12"

Meeting prep (standup 10:30) bullets:
- quick summary of overnight p99 noise and current experiments
- request 1/2 hour with infra to look at nvlink counters if E2 doesn't reduce p99
- propose adding eviction histogram to next sprint (Q2 backlog)

End of capture. If I get a clean repro I'll move this to a mini bug report + add concrete perf artifacts. For now, leave this as the one-page shortwave checklist so the next person can pick up fast.

-- Beatrice
